description: Source gap analysis, missing culinary parameters, and unverified preparations for lamb across NotebookLM sources.
summary_of_gaps: While the notebook sources thoroughly document slow-cooked bone-in roasts (leg and shoulder), gourmet stuffed saddle, and sous-vide loin chops, significant gaps exist for everyday quick-cooking methods (stovetop pan-searing of raw chops), ground lamb preparations, bone-in grilling, and braised shanks/stew cuts.

known_facts_in_sources.safe_temperature: 160°F internal temperature per FDA Safe Minimum Internal Temperatures chart

source.name: SAFE MINIMUM INTERNAL TEMPERATURES as measured with a food thermometer - FDA

missing_from_sources: No cooking method (pan-fry, grill, bake, broil) is documented for ground lamb patties, meatballs, or loose mince.
No pan temperature, oven temperature, or cook times are provided.
No recipes, seasoning ratios, or starch/vegetable pairings specific to ground lamb exist in the sources.
uncovered_cuts.app_recommendation: The app should flag that internal sources lack ground lamb guidelines and enforce the safe minimum 160°F internal temperature standard.

uncovered_cuts.cut: lamb chops (bone-in loin chops, rib chops, cutlets)

known_facts_in_sources.sous_vide_method: Water bath at 118°F–120°F for 1.5–2 hours (1-inch thick), followed by paper-towel drying and 30–60 second cast-iron sear per side.
known_facts_in_sources.aromatics: Rosemary, garlic, cracked black peppercorns (Colorado lamb chops reference).

sources.name: Perfect Sous Vide Steak Recipe (Time & Temp Guide) - Fit Foodie Finds

missing_from_sources: No standalone stovetop pan-searing or pan-basting instructions for raw chops from start to finish.
No direct grilling times or grate temperatures for bone-in rib chops or loin chops.
No baking or broiling times for chops.
uncovered_cuts.app_recommendation: If users input raw lamb chops for stovetop or grill without sous-vide equipment, the app must note that notebook sources only verified precision sous-vide followed by a quick sear.

missing_from_sources: No roasting temperatures, sear-first vs reverse-sear methods, or oven roasting times for whole or frenched racks of lamb.
No herb crust or breadcrumb coating specifications.
uncovered_cuts.app_recommendation: App needs general culinary rules or external fallback parameters if users select rack of lamb.

uncovered_cuts.cut: lamb shanks and stew meat (neck / shoulder chunks)
missing_from_sources: No braising times, liquid-to-meat ratios, or simmering temperatures for individual lamb shanks or diced stew meat.
Sources only cover whole bone-in shoulder (3.5–4 lbs) and whole leg (4–6 lbs).
uncovered_cuts.app_recommendation: App cannot directly scale whole shoulder/leg 3-hour braises down to individual shanks or diced stew cuts without general braising rules.

uncovered_cooking_methods.gap_description: No direct pan-searing times or temperatures exist for raw lamb cuts (steaks, chops, or medallions). Pan searing is only mentioned as a brief 4–5 minute pre-sear before roasting a rolled saddle, or as a 30–60 second post-sous-vide crust sear.
Grilling is only documented for boneless fillet steaks cut from the leg (3–4 minutes per side for salad presentation). No grilling guidelines exist for bone-in chops, skewers/kebabs, or racks.
Broiling is not mentioned or timed for any lamb cut across all notebook sources.
Stir-frying thinly sliced lamb (e.g. with scallions or cumin) is completely absent from notebook sources.
No poaching or stovetop simmering rules exist for lamb; moist-heat cooking is limited to covered oven braising.

unresolved_disagreements_and_temperature.issue: Safe internal temperature vs culinary doneness
unresolved_disagreements_and_temperature.detail: FDA mandates 145°F with a 3-minute rest for whole cuts, whereas culinary sources in the notebook advocate 118°F–120°F (sous vide) and 130°F–135°F (chargrilled steaks). The app rules engine must decide whether to enforce regulatory minimums or chef-recommended medium-rare targets.

unresolved_disagreements_and_temperature.issue: Resting time calculation for large roasts
unresolved_disagreements_and_temperature.detail: WebstaurantStore resting guide gives general rules (5 mins/inch, 10 mins/lb), but RecipeTin Eats roasts specify fixed 15–20 minute resting periods regardless of exact weight.
